metrics.outcome: Done: the site is workable. Every done-when item passes with Audit's evidence and the render check is clean.
metrics.brief: make a website for my friend's cafe called Brew Lab in Bengaluru, with the menu, timings, where it is, a photo gallery and some stories about where their coffee comes from

estimate_vs_charged.name: Header, navigation, menu and site styling
Photo gallery placeholders and coffee stories

review.verdict: A clean, in-role, one-cycle build that met all 8 done-when items in 12 calls and 3.7 minutes, but the brief was too easy to test negotiation, conflicts or rework, and one low-severity defect shipped because the plan left no budget reserve.

identity.note: Asked all four needed questions in one round [2], waited, then declared done on Audit's evidence [22]. Minor gap: the message to the Requester does not mention Audit's duplicate title/charset warning [21].

adaptation.note: Proposed once, merged the work into 3 workflows within the 35 budget and flagged the missing fix reserve [7]. The split put W-1's nav check on sections owned by W-2 and W-3, so that check could not pass on W-1's run [10][12].

priority.note: Granted all three at the full ask with a stated reason and repeated the no-reserve warning [8]. Envelope checks were short and correct [11][14][17]. Because nothing was countered, we cannot tell whether this is judgement or a rubber stamp.

coordination.note: Stated its scheduling rule and spotted the cross-workflow nav dependency [10]. It caught that late, after registration. It also repeated near-identical messages three times [10][13][16] and told builders how to spend retries.

audit.note: Found a real defect that the code check missed (duplicate title and meta charset) and rated it low [21]. It strayed into budget talk ('a fix (8) is not funded'), which belongs to Priority.

W-1.note: Wrote the title, h1, nav, six exact menu items and CSS, and reported honestly that four nav links were unresolved until later sections landed [12]. Who created the duplicate head tags is not shown.

W-2.note: Stayed in its section and delivered hours, address, tap-to-call and a directions link, with an accurate report [15].

W-3.note: Delivered 6 labelled placeholders (2 cafe, 2 food, 2 drinks) and exactly three stories using only supplied details [18].

went_well: No redirects, invalid moves, validator refusals or conflicts across all agents (metrics).
Identity's single question round got everything needed, and the charter turned the brief into 8 checkable items [2][4].
Honest reporting: W-1 and Coordination named the failing nav check up front instead of hiding it [10][12].
The code render check at 360px and 1280px was clean, and Audit's verdict agreed with it [20][21].
problems: The test did not exercise much: 0 counters, 0 refusals, 0 conflicts, 0 retries, 0 holds, no rework, no lessons saved. Evidence on those parts of J2 is absent.
Spend equalled estimate exactly for all three workflows (15, 10, 10) because of the rate card. This says nothing about how well Adaptation estimates cost.
The whole budget was planned away (35/35) [7], so Audit's low-severity warning shipped unfixed [21]. It is cheap and reversible, but the fix path went untested.
W-1's completion check depended on W-2 and W-3 output [10]. The validator did not catch this (0 refusals).
The code check did not detect duplicate head tags. Only Audit's reading did [20][21].
Coordination's messages [10][13][16] repeat the same rule with little new information.
learnings: Change: keep a completion check inside the workflow's own section, or put the nav in the last workflow. Evidence: [10][12].
Change: add a code check for duplicate title and meta tags, since it is deterministic and cheap. Evidence: [20][21].
Test next: the same brief with a budget of about 43 or more, to exercise the Audit to Adaptation to rework to lesson path, which this run never reached.
Test next: a brief with a missing fact, a conflicting ask or a tight budget, so COUNTER, REFUSE, Identity rulings and validator refusals actually fire. Run it with lesson memory on (it was off here).
Test system: report real or measured cost beside the rate card, or the estimate-vs-charged metric stays uninformative.
Keep: registration-order scheduling with one writer under a lock, and Adaptation's habit of flagging the missing reserve early [7].
Consider: Identity's done message should list any open Audit warnings. Evidence: [21] vs [22]; thin, one case.
